analysis: The only change in this PR is test-only: ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift head lines 189-229 add `theDaemonStateReportsTheFilterACommittedSwitchApplied`. It checks that the daemon state.json written by `writeDaemonState()` reports `enabled_models_at_start` and `enabled_models_at_last_switch`. After an accepted switch the latter is ["new-model"]. After a refused commit it is absent and the config is restored to ["old-model"]. The test uses a MockCoordinator with the validate, commit and rollback ack flow. It writes a temp-dir state file and a synthetic snapshot. It adds no production code, no secrets, no network or endpoint changes, and no new attack surface. The rest of the file is unchanged context, including the model-switch drain, lifecycle and rollback tests. I found no weakening of the controls tied to TB-002 (coordinator WebSocket), TB-003 and T-053 (stale authorization). The unchanged tests still assert that registration happens once, that admission is closed during failed or unconfirmed commits, and that a late hash completion cannot publish. The production change that makes the daemon state report the applied filter is not in the supplied evidence. Its handling of the state-file path and permissions, and whether `status` consumers trust the self-reported filter, are unverified. That is a coverage limit, not a finding. T-041 was supplied as context, but nothing in this test touches the prefix cache.
